title: Exact t-exact functor descent on common-stage pair categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $I$ be its directed set of finite subextensions [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. For each $E\in I$ let $\mathcal C_E,\mathcal D_E$ be triangulated categories [def-weil-triangulated-category] with bounded t-structures [def-weil-t-structure]. Supply exact t-exact transitions $U_{L/E},V_{L/E}$ with identity and associative tower comparisons. Form their additive pair categories $P_C,P_D$: objects are $(E,X)$ and Hom groups are the directed colimits of common-stage Hom groups [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups], with transport and composition using the given associators. Explicitly a representative $u:U_{L/E}X\to U_{L/F}Y$ represents an arrow $(E,X)\to(F,Y)$; representatives agree if their transports agree at some larger field. Assume $P_C,P_D$ are triangulated, shifts are induced at a stage, and their distinguished triangles are exactly the isomorphism closures of finite-stage distinguished triangles. Assume they have bounded t-structures whose halves are the isomorphism closures of the finite-stage halves. Write $J_E^C:X\mapsto(E,X)$ and $J_E^D$ for the stage inclusions, with the identity-field identifications.

Let $F_E:\mathcal C_E\to\mathcal D_E$ be exact t-exact functors with specified shift comparisons $c_{E,X}:F_E(X[1])\simeq(F_EX)[1]$. Supply natural isomorphisms $b_{L/E}:V_{L/E}F_E\simeq F_LU_{L/E}$ compatible with shifts, identities and towers: writing $a^C,a^D$ for the transition associators,
$$b_{M/E}(a^D_{M,L,E}F_E)=(F_Ma^C_{M,L,E})(b_{M/L}U_{L/E})V_{M/L}(b_{L/E}).$$
Then
$$F(E,X)=(E,F_EX),\quad F[L,u]=[L,b_{L/F,Y}^{-1}F_L(u)b_{L/E,X}]$$
defines an additive functor $P_C\to P_D$ independent of representatives and common field, without faithfulness of the transitions. It has the natural shift comparison represented at $(E,X)$ by $c_{E,X}$. With this shift comparison $F$ is exact and t-exact. Every $J_E^C,J_E^D$ is also exact and t-exact. The identifications $FJ_E^C=J_E^DF_E$ respect shifts, and after extension to $L$ the identifications are given by $b_{L/E}$.

proof.text: Use the given identity-field identifications throughout (so the identity transitions and their unit comparisons are identities). Apply [lem-sbc-coherent-pair-functor-descent] with $\mathcal A_E=\mathcal C_E$, $\mathcal B_E=\mathcal D_E$, $\Phi_E=F_E$, and the specified $b$. Its associator direction and tower equation are exactly those in the statement; exact functors are additive in the convention of [def-weil-triangulated-category]. The index is the same small directed set of finite intermediate fields. The pair Hom transport and composition are precisely the ones in that lemma. Its conclusion gives the asserted additive functor, with exactly $F[L,u]=[L,b_{L/F,Y}^{-1}F_L(u)b_{L/E,X}]$, independent of representatives and field. The lemma has no faithfulness hypothesis, so none is used here.

source.place: Proposition prop:pseudocone-functor; use the existing generic additive diagram-to-diagram descent lemma.

proof.text:
Write $s^C_{L/E,X}:U_{L/E}(X[1])\simeq(U_{L/E}X)[1]$ and $s^D$ for the transition shift comparisons; with identity transitions they are identities. Shifts induced at a stage means $(E,X)[1]=(E,X[1])$ and $[M,u][1]=[M,(s^C_{M/F,Y})^{-1}u[1]s^C_{M/E,X}]$, and likewise in $P_D$. Put
$$d^A_X=F_L(s^C_{L/E,X})\,b_{L/E,X[1]}:V_{L/E}F_E(X[1])\to F_L((U_{L/E}X)[1]),\qquad d^B_X=(b_{L/E,X})[1]\,s^D_{L/E,F_EX}:V_{L/E}((F_EX)[1])\to(F_LU_{L/E}X)[1].$$
The assumed shift compatibility of $b$ is $c_{L,U_{L/E}X}d^A_X=d^B_XV_{L/E}(c_{E,X})$. Define $\gamma_{(E,X)}=[E,c_{E,X}]:F((E,X)[1])\to(F(E,X))[1]$, with inverse $[E,c_{E,X}^{-1}]$ by common-stage composition [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. For an arrow $[M,u]:(E,X)\to(F,Y)$ compute both sides of the naturality square at the stage $M$, where the components are transported to $V_{M/E}(c_{E,X})$, $V_{M/F}(c_{F,Y})$ (the associators with a repeated field are identities). By the representative formula, $F([M,u][1])$ is represented by $(d^A_Y)^{-1}F_M(u[1])d^A_X$ and $(F[M,u])[1]$ by $(d^B_Y)^{-1}F_M(u)[1]d^B_X$. Then
$$V(c_{F,Y})(d^A_Y)^{-1}F_M(u[1])d^A_X=(d^B_Y)^{-1}c_{M,U Y}F_M(u[1])d^A_X=(d^B_Y)^{-1}F_M(u)[1]c_{M,UX}d^A_X=(d^B_Y)^{-1}F_M(u)[1]d^B_XV(c_{E,X}),$$
using shift compatibility for $Y$, naturality of $c_M$, and shift compatibility for $X$. So $\gamma$ is a natural isomorphism $F\circ[1]\simeq[1]\circ F$. Only the stated equations at one common stage are used; no tower coherence of shift-composite families and no faithfulness.

proof.text: For either system, $J_E$ sends a morphism $u$ to $[E,u]$. Thus $J_E(1)=1$, $J_E(vu)=J_E(v)J_E(u)$ and $J_E(u+v)=J_E(u)+J_E(v)$ directly from common-stage composition and addition [def-weil-directed-colimit-abelian-groups]. Its shift comparison is the identity-field identification $J_E(X[1])\simeq(J_EX)[1]$, natural because shifting $[E,u]$ gives $[E,u[1]]$. A distinguished stage triangle maps to its defining finite-stage triangle, hence is distinguished in the pair category by hypothesis. Consequently every $J_E^C,J_E^D$ is exact by [def-weil-triangulated-category].

proof.text: For $u:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal C_E$, $b_{E/E}=1$ makes the functor formula $F[E,u]=[E,F_Eu]$. On objects it gives $(E,F_EX)$, so $FJ_E^C=J_E^DF_E$. On $X[1]$ the shift comparison of each composite is exactly $[E,c_{E,X}]$, proving compatibility with shifts. In particular, for a distinguished triangle $T=(X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{w}X[1])$ at $E$, its image under $FJ_E^C$ is $J_E^D(F_EX\xrightarrow{F_Eu}F_EY\xrightarrow{F_Ev}F_EZ\xrightarrow{c_{E,X}F_Ew}(F_EX)[1])$. This is distinguished because $F_E$ is exact and Step 3 makes $J_E^D$ exact. Every distinguished triangle of $P_C$ is isomorphic to such a stage image by assumption. Applying $F$ to its triangle isomorphism gives a triangle isomorphism, including its last square by the naturality of Step 2. Isomorphism invariance of distinguished triangles [def-weil-triangulated-category] therefore proves exactness of $F$.

source.place: Tag 014V, definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories; exactness checked on the assumed finite-stage generators of distinguished triangles.

proof.text: Here t-exact means preservation of both halves at zero, equivalently of all their integer translates. If $K\in P_C^{\le0}$, the half hypothesis gives $K\simeq J_E^CX$ for some $X\in\mathcal C_E^{\le0}$. Then $FK\simeq J_E^DF_EX$ lies in $P_D^{\le0}$, because $F_E$ preserves that half and its stage image belongs to the corresponding target half. The identical argument with $\ge0$ proves preservation of the other half. Each $J_E$ preserves both halves directly by their prescribed isomorphism-closure description. The halves are strictly full and satisfy $\mathcal T^{\le n}=\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n}=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-n]$ [def-weil-t-structure]; iterating the shift comparisons, with inverses for negative shifts, gives preservation at every cutoff. This proves all the claimed t-exactness assertions; no reflection of halves is needed.

source.place: Definition def-weil-t-structure, halves and their translates; apply the assumed finite-stage half descriptions.

proof.text:
For $E\subseteq L$, let $r^C_{L/E,X}:J_E^CX\simeq J_L^CU_{L/E}X$ be the common-stage isomorphism represented by the identity of $U_{L/E}X$, with inverse represented by that same identity in the reverse direction; the composites are identities by the pair composition rule. Define $r^D$ likewise. The representative formula, with target stage $L$, gives
$$F(r^C_{L/E,X})=J_L^D(b_{L/E,X})\,r^D_{L/E,F_EX}.$$
Indeed its representative is $b_{L/L,U_{L/E}X}^{-1}F_L(1)b_{L/E,X}=b_{L/E,X}$. Naturality of $r$ follows by representing both sides at $L$; naturality of the comparison is the given naturality of $b$. Its shift square is exactly the assumed shift square for $b$, and its successive-extension square is exactly the displayed tower equation after the associator identifications. Thus the stage identifications in Step 4 extend via precisely the prescribed $b_{L/E}$, respecting shifts and further extension.
